title: Identity assertion window bug causing RBAC drift and missing audit events in private control plane
creator: Priya Desai
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers operating private control planes reported unauthorized access surface changes and gaps in audit logs after an SSO provider rotation and a control-plane upgrade on 2026-03-09. Investigation shows a defect in assertion acceptance logic combined with an intermittent audit ingestion backpressure path. The bug can allow stale SAML assertions (within an expanded replay window) to be applied to the RBAC mapping code, producing role drift for sessions created shortly after identity provider (IdP) rotations. Additionally, when the assertion handling path retries, a burst of small audit events can be dropped upstream by the audit buffer under backpressure, resulting in missing events for affected sessions.
root_cause: Incorrect handling of the assertion "replay_window" and clock-skew normalization in the private control plane led to accepted assertions that had been reissued by the IdP during a rotation. RBAC role-binding code applies mappings on assertion accept; because the rotation introduced transiently duplicated assertions, some sessions picked up stale role mappings. Separately, the audit ingestion service lacked proper backpressure shedding and metric-aligned retries, causing a subset of low-size audit events to be dropped instead of queued.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private control plane with SAML IdP that has short-lived assertion rotation (test IdP provided in confluence doc).
2) Trigger a rotation of assertion tokens at the IdP while simultaneously sending login flows from a scripted client with slight clock skew (+/- 6s).
3) Observe session creation logs where assertion acceptance occurs after rotation and check applied RBAC bindings in the control plane audit logs.
4) Simulate audit ingestion backpressure by limiting consumer throughput and observe dropped audit events in the pipeline metrics and the audit-store.
5) Reproduce in a private cluster staging environment using the provided harness (link in attachments).
mitigation: Applied a temporary policy to tighten the assertion acceptance window on affected private clusters and enabled defensive deduplication at the RBAC application layer. Increased audit buffer capacity and added immediate alerting on audit-drop rates. Notified impacted customers with a timeline and provided mitigations for session re-issue. These mitigations are live on customer clusters as of 2026-03-12 21:30 UTC.
infra_changes: 1) Add strict assertion timestamp normalization and reject assertions outside 5s window by default for private clusters; 2) Add idempotent RBAC bind step keyed by assertion_id to avoid double-application; 3) Expand audit ingestion queue length and add prioritized retry for small audit events.
qa_checks: Validation tests for assertion acceptance window across clock skews - automated unit and integration tests added
E2E SSO flows with IdP rotation in staging cluster
Load test for audit ingestion under simulated backpressure to verify zero dropped events
Manual verification with affected customer accounts that role mapping is restored
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy hotfix to two canary private clusters (non-prod) and run the E2E harness for 1 hour. Phase 2: Canary to three customer pilot clusters (low-risk) with monitoring for 4 hours. Phase 3: Gradual rollout to remaining private clusters over 24 hours with automated rollback on audit-drop or SLO regressions. Notify SRE and Customer Success ahead of each phase and schedule a post-deploy check-in.
postmortem_notes: Preliminary lessons: (a) assertion acceptance logic assumed IdP rotations were non-overlapping; should have included replay-idempotency. (b) audit pipeline lacked SLO-based throttling causing silent drops. Action items: add assertion-idempotency, add chaos tests for IdP rotation, implement SLO-based backpressure handling for audit ingestion, and update runbook for private cluster IdP rotations.
